hypotheses.claim: A durable single-host lease needs three separately bound facts: monotonic or boottime interval validity within one boot, explicit boot identity across restart, and generation fencing after takeover; wall time may be audit data but must not alone mint expiry authority.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Generation fencing plus ordinary CLOCK_REALTIME expiry is sufficient because a newer generation immediately fences the old worker and host clock jumps are operationally negligible.
hypotheses.discriminator: Run forward/backward realtime discontinuities, suspend, reboot/boot-id change, expiry-boundary renewal, expired-owner self-resurrection, concurrent takeover and stale-generation projection. Preserve liveness as well as single-active safety.
hypotheses.falsifier: A contender acquires before the lease's accepted interval elapsed, an expired owner renews without fresh generation, or a pre-reboot lease is accepted under a new boot identity.

hypotheses.claim: Backlog pressure and worker health are operational signals, not semantic freshness; consequential ClayGraph use requires exact authoritative event-set/root currentness.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: SOFT pressure is sufficiently fresh for low-risk graph use and exact-current gating unnecessarily sacrifices availability.
hypotheses.discriminator: Replay captured and fresh load while lesioning exact-current admission at NONE/SOFT/HARD thresholds; measure stale consequential reads, decisions and recovery amplification by risk class.
hypotheses.falsifier: Any non-exact graph state influences a consequential result without an explicit bounded-staleness contract and producer-owned risk authorization.

hypotheses.claim: Parser evidence must bind both a frozen regression universe and a separately enumerated expanding source universe; a single rolling percentage either rewrites history or hides new unsupported surfaces.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: One current-main coverage percentage is simpler and sufficient if every run is exact-head bound.
hypotheses.discriminator: Append unsupported, supported and modified-existing sources. Require historical metrics to remain identity-stable, existing-source regressions to turn red, and every new source to appear with explicit syntax-family/admission status.
hypotheses.falsifier: A newly rejected source disappears from reporting, or an incompatible change to a frozen source leaves the frontier gate green.

hypotheses.claim: Projection-contract syntax may use a separate composable frontend only if it converges into the same typed IR, WP04 effect/authority admission and evaluator semantics as Structured-V1.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Extending the single Structured-V1 grammar is cheaper and avoids frontend divergence.
hypotheses.discriminator: Inventory the two projection sources, implement diagnostic-only unified-grammar and separate-frontend variants, then compare strict conflicts, AST/IR equivalence, rejection behavior, complexity and identical WP04/effect gates.
hypotheses.falsifier: The separate frontend creates a second authority/effect semantics, or the unified grammar passes all strict/adversarial gates with lower cost and identical IR.

hypotheses.claim: Run-unique checkout is a scoped continuity repair, but reproducible ordinary checkout requires eliminating privileged residue creation and restoring runner-user ownership at the source.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Permanent RUNNER_TEMP isolation is sufficient; persistent workspace cleanliness has no semantic value once exact SHA and cleanup are asserted.
hypotheses.discriminator: Trace root-owned inode creation to workflow/process identity, remove that privilege path, clean the persistent tree, then execute repeated ordinary checkouts and isolated controls with bytecode creation, cancellation and crash injection.
hypotheses.falsifier: Ordinary runner-user checkout remains clean across repeated adversarial runs without removing the privileged source, or isolated trees acquire undeletable foreign-owned residue.
